## A. Real and named — implement these exactly

These held everywhere the audit looked. They are the design system; port them as they are.

### The verdict law

| rule | value |
|---|---|
| a verdict resolves at `T_HOLD + T_IN + T_WAIT + T_TEXT` | 1450 ms (20.3 f) by default |
| then it rests, always the same | `RESULT_HOLD_MS` 2450 ms (34.3 f) |
| the icon fades in and rises 0.97 → 1, both ease-out | within `ARRIVE_MS` 300 ms (4.2 f), never an overshoot |
| the caption fades ease-out, starting exactly at `T_HOLD + T_IN + T_WAIT` | `T_TEXT` 300 ms (4.2 f) |
| no sign is drawn during the hold — first ink lands on the first step after it | every verdict |
| every mechanism sub-phase clears two panel frames | `VERDICT_ACCENT_MIN_MS` 145 ms (2.0 f) |
| a mechanism lengthens `T_WAIT` — never the entrance | law-allowed, documented per module |
| phases resolve per **instance**, not per class | `lock` and `unlock` differ |

### Entering and leaving

- Everything that appears, fades; everything that leaves, fades. The one sanctioned overshoot (`back_out`) is confined to the status flash.
- A screen that owns its canvas (`rests_on_token` False) leaves as **one dimmed picture** on its outgoing alpha spring — verdicts, the PIN row, the explosion and led verdicts all share one code path.
- Sequential swaps never crossfade: the old text fades out, lands on the beat, then the new fades in.
- Corner chevrons never cut during a leg — alpha and angle lerp on the morph spring, including to and from hidden.
- Pulse rings and the static hero pager ride the screen's own alpha, so they enter and leave with its text.

### The transit (seen ~7× per transaction)

- **Every leg takes the same time, whatever the distance** — a 274 px value leg and a zero-distance hero→status leg settle together. One spring profile drives all five channels.
- The disc leads, the words follow: incoming text is released `TEXT_IN_DELAY_MS` 150 ms (2.1 f) after the leg starts, from a single site — fresh leg, mid-flight reversal and rebase alike.
- Position, radius and text alpha stay continuous across a reversal (velocity carried). A press during a leg is **never dropped or queued** — it retargets from the live pose.
- The device uses `NAV`; `KIOSK` reaches demo renders only. No third pace exists.

### Input

| rule | value |
|---|---|
| one hold curve everywhere: flat, then linear to full | 0 until `TAP_MAX_MS` 250 ms (3.5 f), full at `HOLD_COMMIT_MS` 2000 ms (28.0 f) from press-down |
| an early release drains it | `HOLD_SNAPBACK_MS` 200 ms (2.8 f), ease-out, from the level reached |
| nothing of a hold shows for its first 250 ms | so a tap never flashes a partial fill |
| the commit fade is identical on sign and on decline | one leg, one curve |
| decline is armed on every navigable screen; sign only where `commit` | status screens are input-dead (verified by 8 gestures applied during an ending) |
| the ask is the hub; left undoes right on paged details | |
| navigation taps never wait for a double-tap or chord window | only entries do |
| a tap that a chord or double press converts is never shown and taken back | |

### Flow shape

- A segment with `CONFIRM_MIN_DETAILS` (7)+ details takes `Confirm?` at index `CONFIRM_INDEX` (5) — inserted by the design system, never by hand.
- The walk returns to the ask before an ending. Success plays the qubit film and lands a check; a cancel does no work, so it resolves in place with an X; a failure the host reports after dispatch names the film (`anim="qubit"`) and it collides into the X; an ending led by a film arrives.
- Unbranded flows stroke the ending disc in the state colour; branded families fill it.

### The loading film (built after the audit — theme 5)

| rule | value |
|---|---|
| a film starts when the work is dispatched; it is a MINIMUM-length depiction | `REVS` 3 turns of `TURN_MS` 850 ms (11.9 f) on the orbit |
| the steady orbit is the loop region — pixel-periodic in one turn (`L-LOOP` proves it) | `QubitCfg.loop` (2250 ms (31.5 f), 4800 ms (67.2 f)), `loop_ms` 850 ms (11.9 f) |
| while the work is outstanding the pose clock wraps the loop in whole turns; the busy caption runs unwrapped | `loading.film_time`, `StatusAnim.draw_busy` |
| the answer latches the outcome at the spiral — never later than `t6` of the last turn | `StatusAnim.resolve`; `t6` 5800 ms (81.2 f) on the stock film |
| the spiral + flash tail and the rest are fixed | 1400 ms (19.6 f) + `RESULT_HOLD_MS` 2450 ms (34.3 f) |
| a loading that must endure takes more whole turns, never a slower spin | `REVS_LONG` 5 |
| a finished ending freezes forever; an unanswered film loops — there is no timeout | `FlowDriver.answer`, the bench's `y` / `n` |

## B. Real but unnamed — name them, change no pixel

The pattern behind them, in one line each:

- **D1-03** — T_WAIT is hand-summed from three unnamed kinds of time (rest + mechanism + beat); the phase vocabulary exists in 9 modules but not in the base class or the docs
- **D1-07** — Who inherits the verdict law vs who copies its numbers: ArriveStatus, the hold_to_confirm cancel tail and pin_entering's handoff re-type it; sig_error re-types draw(); three modules re-draw the same arriving disc
- **D10-12** — The panel rate lives only in prose: '14 fps' / 'panel frame' appears at 12+ sites, no PANEL_FPS or frame-ms token; frame-derived values are hand-rounded from 145
- **D11-01** — 14 fps exists only in prose and --fps defaults: no PANEL_FPS / FRAME_MS token, so the frame period is re-derived three incompatible ways
- **D2-13** — Uncodified: the Sim's navigation in/out grammar - a circle group that leads on the morph spring and a text group that trails by 150 ms on the alpha spring; nothing scales
- **D4-11** — Film / token geometry literals duplicated across loading.py, burst.py, status.py, headshake.py (1.2 ring inset x4, 2.4 ring width x2, 44.0, 0.22, 5 followers, 0.8 px, metaball bound)
- **D5-02** — Uncodified: every leg of every kind takes exactly the same time, and each element rides a fixed channel - the 'leg anatomy' is nowhere written as a rule
- **D7-08** — Uncodified: rejected / unbound input is ALWAYS silent (no shake, no flash) - six cases agree, only one is written as a rule
- **D8-12** — ArriveStatus re-declares the verdict phases and inlines the entrance pair; LedAnim.HANDOFF_MS is linked to VerdictAnim.T_HOLD by comment only
- **G13-01** — No completion signal anywhere: every film is a closed timeline and the ending is chosen before it starts
- **G13-02** — The loop seam is real and pixel-exact: the steady orbit repeats every 850 ms, so only the 1400 ms tail is fixed
- **G13-03** — The outcome seam is t6 (the spiral's end): every frame before it is outcome-independent, but nothing can latch the outcome
- **G13-08** — The system's current answer to 'the work takes an unknown time' is a build-time guess in whole turns - written twice, and unavailable to the qubit film
- **G14-04** — Answer to (a)/(c): the stacking is not an accident — the repo's alpha idiom makes the disc-last order the only possible one, and that reason is written nowhere
- **G15-01** — The stagger / lead-lag family is real but unnamed: 6 sites, 5 unlinked values, no token, no rule, and CHEV_STAGGER is the one member nothing in the docs or the audit ever names
- **X1-01** — The panel has one true amplitude floor (alpha 0.0137) and a 4-level pure-green band above it; the code's 54 ad-hoc floors sit around it by accident, and one is on the wrong side
- **X2-02** — There is a codified TIME floor for accents and no displacement ceiling at all — the per-frame step spans 0.25 to 96.5 px with nothing naming a limit
- **X2-05** — The follower chain is the only thing keeping a 96 px-per-frame token step from reading as a cut, and the invariant that makes it work is nowhere stated as a rule

## C. Deliberate character — do not normalise

17 differences survived measurement as real and either invisible or already decided more than once by the owner. Porting them 'consistently' would change the feel.

- **D11-02** — The verdict entrance law renders 4 or 5 poses and starts at alpha 0.07 / 0.26 / 0.32 / 0.00 depending only on the preceding T_HOLD's sub-frame offset  
  _A 300 ms fade rendering four poses instead of five, opening at alpha 0.26 instead of 0, is not something anyone sees once, let alone tells apart between screens. Re-cutting four phase constants into 428.57 and 285.71 to chase it makes every number in the port ugly for no visible return; the useful half of this finding is D10-12's 'quote beats in frames'._
- **D11-08** — Repeating periods split in two: the 500-ms family is frame-locked forever, while 4100 / 8600 / 3600 drift through a five-step sub-frame cycle — so a page flip's dead window is 2 or 3 frames depending on which page you are on  
  _28.6 ms of sub-frame drift on a dwell timer is invisible — the only place it ever showed was the page flip, and that gets fixed at the flip. Typing 4071.43 into a design token to chase this panel's grid ports worse than 4100; quantize at the scheduler if you ever need it._
- **D11-11** — A 71.43 ms frame grid is adoptable in one pass: no timing value in the system would move by more than half a panel frame, and 14 of them are already on it  
  _The grid is real, but re-typing 48 values by up to half a frame changes nothing anyone can see and churns every number the port has to cross-check. Write it as guidance for new tokens; do not run the migration._
- **D3-05** — Four power-deceleration exponents for one purpose (2.4 / 2.6 / 2.8 / 3.0); freewheel's only caller re-declares its default  
  _Seven degrees mid-tumble and under two pixels — these exponents came from separately tuned source art and nobody will ever see the difference. Leave them; the only thing worth touching is factory_signing re-declaring freewheel's own default._
- **D3-16** — Expanding rings: all four fade linearly (uncodified); three grow linearly, the blast grows on decel  
  _Four rings fade linearly because brightness tracks distance and the blast decelerates because a shock wave does — that's physics, not drift. A linear() wrapper is ceremony; one sentence in DESIGN.md is all this deserves._
- **D4-09** — 'One sweep cycle' = 5000 ms is declared four times; BAND_SWAP_MS 5000 is a coincidence  
  _Tying HERO_DWELL to SWEEP_PERIOD_MS cements a claim that is not true — the sweep starts a second late, so a 5000 ms dwell shows 0.8 of a cycle. Leave the four 5000s and delete the 'one full sweep' comment instead._
- **D5-14** — A film's side entrance is hard-wired to the DEMO pace: ENTER_MS 800 and spring_travel(profile=KIOSK) also play on device, where the legs around it run NAV  
  _No flow uses a side entrance and none is planned; the path is reachable only through the CLI. Derive ENTER_MS the day a flow needs it — spending pre-port budget on a code path that has never shipped a frame is how ports run late._
- **D6-10** — hold_to_confirm's 'scaled-down idle sweep' shares only the period and amplitude with the real sweep: raw sine, no 1000 ms centred hold, opposite first direction, no trail, and a scripted 300 ms recentre instead of the tau-chase  
  _The library screen's drift is a pure function of t so the screen stays seekable — that's a real reason, and at 11.9 px nobody is holding it up against the Sim's sweep. Stop calling it "a scaled-down idle sweep" in the docstring and leave the motion alone._
- **D6-14** — PIN instruction-label pulse: a documented user cadence (3 s on / 3 s off, one hint at a time) whose tokens live only in the screen and whose clock ignores input  
  _The 3-on/3-off cadence is settled, documented twice and has exactly one screen. Promoting it to a system rule before a second entry screen exists is inventing a family out of one member — and the hint correctly does not animate per keystroke, which is the part that mattered._
- **D9-05** — Ending vocabulary is ad hoc: 7 success keys, 4 cancel keys, and the skill's own rule fits 8 of 20 unbranded flows  
  _Seven words for one idea is untidy, but these are captions the owner wrote and likes, and re-keying shipped endings churns folder names and every GIF for zero motion gain. The ask-verb rule already exists in the skill — hold new flows to it and leave the shipped ones alone._
- **D9-14** — CLI output grammar: top-level flows and family flows name their plain render differently; the list and the manifest count screens differently; the README's --early example cannot run  
  _The naming split shows on five files, nothing downstream parses the path, and renaming 85 renders plus the README the week before a port is pure churn. Fix the one README example that cannot run and move on._
- **G13-10** — QubitStatus and ResolveStatus type their preview instants as absolute ms where eight sibling anims derive them - the two that break first if t_resolve moves  
  _A preview is a contact sheet, not a law, and 3500 against 3475 is a third of a panel frame. If t_resolve ever moves, you will re-pick the stills by eye anyway._
- **G14-03** — Answer to (b): gating the incoming text on the disc clearing its column is statically decidable and costs 0.6 panel frames on average — but it breaks the one-leg-one-duration invariant  
  _Gating the incoming text on the disc clearing its column buys 0.6 of a frame on average and costs the only property the Sim guarantees — that every leg takes the same time. Leave the 150 ms; keep the occlusion budget as a regression check and nothing more._
- **G17-01** — The Ethereum mark is the deliberate fallback for an unresolved icon (owner decision)  
  _The owner has ruled: on an EthereumPhone the ether mark is the honest answer for art the device cannot resolve, and it is already documented as the intent on batch-sign. Measurement backs it — pin/unlock never rasterises the mark at all and there is not one live typo in thirty flows. Catch typos in the repo, leave the device behaviour alone._
- **G17-08** — The icon-to-gradient coupling exists in code but has no live instance (refuted on every screen)  
  _Measured to zero live instances: the ramp that icon would pick is never the ramp that draws. A coupling with no instance is a note for whoever adds the seventh screen, not a fix._
- **X1-06** — The busy caption's breath holds fully black for four consecutive panel frames (286 ms of every 2000 ms cycle) - the trough is a beat, not an instant  
  _The four dark frames are the breath - a raised cosine that pauses at the bottom is exactly the loading rhythm the owner chose, and the spec exports the curve itself so a port inherits it. Two draws below the floor cost nothing._
- **X2-08** — last_attempt's three mechanism phases each end in a 3-4 frame dead tail — one frame inside T_SETTLE is bit-exactly identical to the one before it  
  _The tail is the linger. A verdict is rare and is allowed to rest inside its own window; trimming phase windows the owner tuned by eye to chase one duplicate frame buys nothing on a 14 fps panel._

## D. Dead — names that read like rules and govern nothing

16 findings. Every one of these looks like a law in the source. **Do not implement any of them.** A dead constant that looks like a bound is exactly what a port turns into a clamp.

- **D3-14** — DESIGN.md's overshoot/vocabulary paragraph has drifted: motion.pop is dead, and 'one overshoot is sanctioned' ignores wobble / heartbeat / attention_pulse
- **D4-12** — Dead / vestigial timing tokens: MOVE_MS, FADE_MS, PRESS_FEEDBACK_MS, motion.pop, burst.HOLD_END, STATUS_DWELL
- **D5-16** — MOVE_MS 900 has no consumer; FADE_MS 180 survives only as hold_to_confirm's private fade - both still documented as the transition's span bound
- **D7-01** — Press-down acknowledgment is specified (PRESS_FEEDBACK_MS 120 ease_out chevron nudge) but never rendered: a tap's only feedback starts on RELEASE
- **D8-09** — burst.HOLD_END 1400 is dead: the standalone explosion dwells RESULT_HOLD_MS 2450 after the boom, not the 1400 its comment claims
- **D9-02** — The loader's status-free return branch is dead, and wrong for intro-led families
- **D9-13** — normalize_screens' side and size defaults are never used - and the side default encodes a rule no flow follows
- **G11-06** — `bind` is a dead switch: in the phase where it is the only thing turning the bridge off, the geometry already had it off by 18 px
- **G12-07** — The `cur` setter is documented as a mid-flow harness seek and no harness uses it: its only two callers in the whole repo are the flow's boot composition and the bench restart
- **G13-07** — The one word the vocabulary has for 'not finished yet' is dead, and default_anim routes it to the CANCEL resolve
- **G17-03** — The documented resolution chain is dead code: `resolve_glyph`'s icon / symbol / monogram branches and VECTOR_SYMBOLS have no caller
- **X2-11** — pq1 has no FRAME_MS, so both motion-blur exposures are derived from the accent floor and are 1.5% off a real panel frame
- **X4-06** — `sweep` is a dead token: zero uses in 1350 normalized screens, published as a common key, and geometrically valid only on a centred circle
- **X5-04** — Four kinds of not-really-live token are exported as scope=device: burst.HOLD_END, motion.pop, 7 stated-contract layout tokens — and their "do not port" rationale is dropped because only trailing comments survive
- **X6-01** — The dead spatial family is 7 names / 5 statements, not 2 — and every one of them is published to the firmware spec as scope "device"
- **X6-02** — SWEEP_X_MIN/MAX is the swept disc's INK EXTENT, computed from the nominal amplitude — the realised extent is 92..335, and nothing clamps anything

The spec now protects you from these automatically: every token in `spec/motion.json` carries a `scope` computed from a reader census — `device`, `demo`, `dead`, `contract` (a stated bound nothing enforces) or `spec-only`. Implement `device`. Ignore `demo` and `dead`. Never turn a `contract` into a clamp.

## E. Fake rules — the code says otherwise

141 findings where a rule is written down, or looks like one, and the code does something else. These are the ones that mislead a port. The worst:

- **G17-07** — Family icon names are registered at import time, so the same screen dict renders the Safe mark or the Ethereum mark depending on whether the family package was imported — and the substituted mark ignores the screen's icon_color
- **X4-01** — Five schema keys are silently dropped on the wrong kind; exactly one misplacement raises
- **X4-03** — `commit` is published as a common key and honoured on every kind, but layout.py's own comment says "never on a detail"
- **D7-02** — A SIGN hold and a DECLINE hold are pixel-identical for the full 2000 ms - the law's 'the pressed side is what the chevrons say' is not drawn
- **X5-02** — motion.json verdict_law flattens the law to four numbers (400/300/450/300) that only 2 of 23 anims obey, with one source line and no override note
- **D9-11** — unlock_batch is the 'worked example' every doc points to, and it follows none of the flow grammar
- **X6-02** — SWEEP_X_MIN/MAX is the swept disc's INK EXTENT, computed from the nominal amplitude — the realised extent is 92..335, and nothing clamps anything
- **D2-01** — A status ending that rests on the token EXITS in one frame (caption, result glyph, ring/fill cut) while token-less screens fade on the alpha spring

Plus one whole class: values that are equal **by luck**, not by link — the same 300 ms declared nine times and linked four, the 400 ms handoff declared three times, the 420 ms shake typed in five modules, `alpha <= 0.01` at 48 sites in 26 files. They agree today. Nothing makes them agree tomorrow.

---

## How to use this

1. Implement **A** exactly — it is the design.
2. Take **B** from the spec's token block, not from the screen you happen to be reading. Where a screen disagrees with a token, the token is right.
3. Leave **C** alone, including the parts that look inconsistent.
4. Implement nothing from **D**. Check `scope` before porting any constant.
5. For **E**, port the behaviour the Python has today and read the report's theme for what is planned — `tools/check/baseline.toml` lists every open item with its finding id.
